newsitem.title: USA: Prudential policyholders to receive legal notice.
newsitem.headline: Prudential policyholders to receive legal notice.

text.p: Millions of Prudential Insurance Co of America policyholders are about to receive a "plain English" legal notice explaining the company's remediation plan, officials said on Friday.

Separate announcements were made by the company that wrote the document and by the New Jersey Department of Banking and Insurance, which heads a task force of insurance regulators from 45 states and the District of Columbia.
The task force was formed to examine sales and marketing practices in the life insurance industry.
Prudential is the largest of a number of insurers charged with deceptive sales practices nationwide.
The notices will be sent to some 7.5 million people in 45 states and the District of Columbia, who bought more than 10.7 million Prudential whole life insurance policies between 1982 and 1995.
Prudential sent an earlier notice related to the remediation program in November of 1996.

But the revised document is significant because it represents one of the few instances in which the parties to a large, class action lawsuit have asked a communications firm to create simplified legal notices, said an executive at the firm that wrote the notice.
"We hope this will start a trend toward simplified, clear language in the financial services world," said Irene Etzkorn, executive vice president at Siegel & Gale.
Siegel & Gale was hired by attorneys for the plaintiffs, and the notice was approved by Prudential and the task force of insurance regulators.
